item.title: Have and has in a packing list
item.explanation_text:
Use have and has to say what someone has for a game or a trip. You can write a short sentence for each person on a packing list. Use have with I, you, we, and they: “We have a ball.” Use have with two or more names too: “Mia and Leo have a ball.” Use has with he, she, it, or one name: “Mia has a towel.” When you choose the verb, look at who has the things. One name still takes has when the person has two things: “Leo has two towels.”

To say that a thing is missing, use don't have with I, you, we, they, or a group of people: “We don't have a spare bag.” Use doesn't have with he, she, it, or one name: “Mia doesn't have a spare bag.” In these sentences about what people have, use have after don't or doesn't.
item.contrast_text: Mia and Leo have a ball. → Mia has a ball. | Mia and Leo don't have a ball. → Mia doesn't have a ball.
item.common_error_pattern: Use has in a yes sentence with he, she, it, or one name. Use have with two names joined by and. In the negative patterns don't have and doesn't have, the main verb stays have.

examples.bad: Lina have a small sports bag.
examples.good: Lina has a small sports bag.

examples.bad: Omar and Lina has a ball.
examples.good: Omar and Lina have a ball.

examples.bad: We doesn't have a spare shirt.
examples.good: We don't have a spare shirt.

children.title: My bag
children.instructions: You are making your own packing list. Fill the gap with have or has.

children.title: Two things, one person
children.instructions: Ben is ready for the game. Fill the gap with have or has.

children.title: A ball for two players
children.instructions: Read the note about two players. Fill the gap with have or has.

children.title: No towel
children.instructions: Ella's towel is at home. Fill the gap with don't have or doesn't have.
children.prompt_text: She ___ a towel for the game.

children.title: No water bottles
children.instructions: You and your friend came without water bottles. Fill the gap with don't or doesn't.

children.title: Check the coach's list
children.instructions: Replace the wrong verb with have or has. Keep the other words.

children.title: Fix the note about socks
children.instructions: Fix the one wrong word after doesn't. Keep the other words.

children.title: Write about one player
children.instructions: Write the sentence about Mei alone. Start with Mei and keep the same item.
children.prompt_text: Mei and Dan have a spare bag.

children.title: Add a player to the note
children.instructions: Replace Ivan with “Ivan and Rosa”. Change the form of have to match. Keep all other words in the same order.
accepted_answers: Ivan and Rosa have a pump.

children.title: Change the list after a check
children.instructions: The players have no snacks. Rewrite the sentence with don't have or doesn't have. Keep the same subject and item words.

children.title: Tell a teammate
children.instructions: Tell your teammate what they have for the game. Start with You. Use each tile once.

children.title: Report a missing item
children.instructions: Say that Jay is missing an item today. Start with Jay and put today last. Use each tile once.
children.prompt_text: have / today / Jay / a jacket / doesn't
accepted_answers: Jay doesn't have a jacket today.
